items.title: 1. Municipal Waste Collection
text: Many cities offer curbside pickup or designated drop-off locations for bulky waste items. Check with your local waste authority for schedules and rules. Some municipalities require booking or special permits.

items.title: 2. Recycling Centers
text: Recycling is one of the best options for old appliances. Many recycling facilities accept appliances such as refrigerators, ovens, and washers, and break them down for scrap metal and reusable parts. This helps reduce landfill waste and supports sustainability.

items.title: 3. Retailer Take-Back Programs
text: When buying new appliances, some retailers offer take-back programs. They’ll pick up your old unit when they deliver the new one. This is convenient, but availability may vary depending on the retailer and your location.

blocks.text: How to Get Rid of Broken Appliances

c: Getting rid of broken appliances requires some planning. You want to ensure disposal is safe, legal, and as eco-friendly as possible. Here’s a step-by-step guide:

items.title: Step 1: Identify Your Appliance
text: Determine what type of appliance you have: fridge, washer, dryer, stove, etc. Some require special handling due to hazardous materials like refrigerants or chemicals.

items.title: Step 2: Research Local Disposal Options
text: Check municipal waste websites or recycling centers to see what they accept. Some programs require you to drop off appliances at a specific location or schedule a pickup.

items.title: Step 3: Consider Junk Removal Services
text: For convenience, call a professional junk removal service like Live Junk Free. We specialize in safely and efficiently disposing of all kinds of appliances. No heavy lifting, no hassle, we handle it all.

items.title: Step 4: Donate if Possible
text: If your appliance is broken but repairable, consider donating it to charity organizations or thrift stores. They may refurbish and reuse the appliance, giving it a second life.

items.title: Step 5: Follow Safety Guidelines
text: Always unplug appliances and remove hazardous materials before disposal. Wear gloves and take proper precautions when moving heavy items.
